source_read: https://www.honipoke.com/nutritional-calculator (rendered fresh in Chromium 2026-10-08: every row of the three tabs clicked and the detail panel read by innerText and by screenshot), 20 /menu/<dish> pages, 4 listing pages and /allergens (all fetched fresh, robots.txt has no Disallow)
not_verifiable: allergens: none published (link only): the chain's allergen matrix and its own dish pages disagree (California page lists gluten, matrix does not; Sriracha Mayo Salmon matrix lists crustaceans, page does not), and several calculator dishes have no matrix row, so there was nothing safe to compare or publish
notes: All 26 calculator rows (20 published + 6 held back) match the fresh read on kcal, protein, carbs, fat, fibre, sodium and the table's whole numbers; the 6 held-back dishes are exactly the 6 whose dish page prints a Cal figure (450/450/450/400/300/500 vs calculator 638/572/659/542/507/836), already held by the script, not new; the 14 other dish pages print no Cal. Vegetarian tags (Avocado & Mango, Tofu Teriyaki, Green Zen Tofu) match the chain's own icon on its listing pages; contains_beef on Shoyu Paitan Beef Ramen is right. Re-run of honi_poke.py on the fresh pages reproduces data/source byte for byte. Systematic finding: the calculator's script multiplies its totals (kcal x0.85, protein x1.10, carbs x0.90, fat x0.90) while the ingredient kcal list beside each total is unscaled, so every dish's headline kcal is 14-15% below the sum of the ingredient kcal printed next to it and kcal differs from 4P+4C+9F by up to 21%; copied as the chain prints it (below the 30% hold line), and note.txt now says so in plain words (the only change made: the old note did not mention the 15%). 6 audit flags marked ok (2 energy-gap, 4 sodium-very-high: ramen print 2818-6142 mg). Founder call: whether to keep this chain published at all, given its only source is a calculator that does not add up its own list.
